issues.title: out-link-pattern starting with '/' is silently mangled by Git Bash (MSYS path conversion), breaking the documented crawl example on Windows

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: From Git Bash on Windows: ./b4w.ps1 crawl "http://localhost:18080/generated/crawl/index.html" -d 2 -ol "a.product" -olp "/product/"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Crawl discovers the 9 product pages and excludes category/anchor links (as the crawl --help example and task instructions promise).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Crawl completes successfully with '1 pages found' (only the seed page) and NO error or diagnostic — 0 links discovered. A diagnostic appears only for some patterns: using -olp "/generated/crawl/product" prints 'the out-link pattern 'C:/Program Files/Git/generated/crawl/product' filtered them all', proving MSYS converted the leading-slash argument into a Windows path before it reached the backend. The same command via ./b4w.sh works (9 pages).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: MSYS2/Git Bash path conversion rewrites arguments starting with '/' (e.g. '/product/') into Windows paths ('C:/Program Files/Git/product/') before the b4w.ps1/pwsh boundary. The regex then matches nothing. Quoting the argument does not prevent this. b4w.sh survives because its bash wrapper passes arguments through differently. The failure is silent because 0 matched links is a legitimate crawl outcome ('No links found (depth >= 1) completes with 0 pages' per crawl.md). The crawl --help example '-olp "/product/"' is exactly the broken form.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (crawl examples); skills/browser4-cli/references/shell-quoting.md; skills/browser4-cli/references/crawl.md

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Change the crawl --help and crawl.md examples to use a leading-slash-free pattern (e.g. -olp "product/") or the safe ""\".*?/product/"""" form on Windows
- Document in shell-quoting.md that MSYS converts arguments starting with '/', and that b4w.sh or pwsh direct invocation is required for -olp patterns with leading slashes
- In b4w.ps1, export MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL="*" (or equivalent) before invoking pwsh so slash-leading args pass through unmangled
- Emit a diagnostic (like the existing 'filtered them all' message) whenever 0 links survive the out-link-pattern filter — the current silent completion hides the problem

issues.title: Swarm backend unavailable in dev mode: swarm query fails with 503 'Swarm not installed' and no documented fix

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. Start dev backend via ./b4w.ps1 (auto-starts locally built bundle). 2. ./b4w.ps1 swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS. 3. ./b4w.ps1 swarm query --sql @query.sql --seed-file urls.txt --refresh

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Swarm jobs run against the local backend, as the SKILL.md §4b decision tree and swarm.md quick start imply for the parallel path.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: swarm query fails with HTTP 503 {"error":"Swarm not installed","message":"Swarm backend is not installed. Install the browser4-swarm plugin and restart the server."}. swarm create succeeds (it is CLI-side) but no jobs can run. The dev runtime bundle (browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/target/runtime-bundle/...) has an empty plugins/ directory. swarm.md documents the 503 but not how to enable the plugin in a dev-mode setup. Manual fix that worked: copy browser4-plugins/browser4-swarm/target/browser4-swarm-4.14.0-rc.3.jar into <bundle>/plugins/ and restart the backend (~10 min).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The runtime-bundle build script stages plugin JARs (build-runtime-bundle.ps1 line ~951 copies the swarm JAR), but the dev bundle used by the daemon was built earlier without plugins and is not refreshed when source changes — the daemon rebuilds the server libs but not the bundle's plugins/ dir ('Installed bundle: v4.14.0-rc.2' vs server 4.14.0-rc.3). First-time dev users have no documented path to enable swarm.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/build-runtime-bundle.ps1 (plugin staging); cli/browser4-cli/src/daemon.rs (bundle freshness/rebuild decision); skills/browser4-cli/references/swarm.md (missing dev-mode setup instructions)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a 'Dev mode' section to swarm.md explaining the plugin requirement and the exact copy-JAR-into-bundle-plugins + restart procedure
- Make the daemon stage missing plugin JARs from browser4-plugins/*/target/*.jar when starting a dev backend, or rebuild the bundle when plugins are absent
- Surface a more actionable CLI error: when swarm is unavailable, point to plugin list / the dev-mode install step instead of just 'Swarm not installed'

issues.title: Crawl result reports pages discovered in later waves with depth=1 instead of their true depth

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. ./b4w.sh crawl "http://localhost:18080/generated/crawl/index.html" -d 2 -ol "a.product" -olp "/product/" (via b4w.sh). 2. ./b4w.ps1 crawl result <task-id>

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Pages directly linked from the seed should be depth=1 and pages linked from those pages depth=2 (products 4-9 are only reachable via product pages 1-3, which link to 4.html/5.html etc.).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: All 9 product pages are reported with "depth" : 1 in the result payload, even though 6 of them (products 4-9) are 2 hops from the seed — the hub page contains only 3 product links. The depth cap still behaved correctly: the depth-3 page (depth3/8.html, linked from product/4.html) was NOT fetched, so internal depth tracking is correct and only the reported depth field is wrong.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Likely an off-by-one (or wave-index vs graph-depth mix-up) in the crawl result builder that assigns each discovered page the depth of the wave that enqueued it rather than its true distance from the seed. Needs verification in CrawlService's page-record construction.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/api/service/CrawlService.kt (page depth attribution in result)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Compute depth as distance from the seed (parent depth + 1) when recording pages in the result payload
- Add a test asserting depth values for a 3-level fixture graph (hub -> product -> related -> depth3)
- If depth is intentionally wave-relative, document that semantics in crawl.md instead of implying graph depth

issues.title: Documented global short flag '-q' is rejected when placed after a command, with a misleading 'unexpected positional arguments' error

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: From Git Bash: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot -q  (also page-info -q, goto <url> -q)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: -q is documented as a global option ('-q, --quiet — suppress normal output'); it should be accepted after the command like --quiet is.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Error: error: unexpected positional arguments (this command accepts none): ["-q"] (goto says 'accepts 1'). Placing -q before the command (./b4w.ps1 --quiet htmlsnapshot) works, and --quiet after the command works. A first-time user writing `htmlsnapshot -q` (natural flag position) gets a confusing error that calls a documented flag a positional argument.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI's argument parser only recognizes short global flags before the command word; after the command, '-q' falls through to the subcommand's positional parser, which reports it as an unexpected positional. The error message does not hint that -q is a valid global flag.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (global flag parsing / rewrite_prefixed_command); cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (command arg definitions)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Accept -q (and other documented global short flags) in any position, or at minimum special-case the error: 'unknown option -q (global flags must precede the command: browser4-cli -q htmlsnapshot)'
- Make the parser treat unknown dashed tokens as unknown options instead of positional arguments

issues.title: Backend restart in dev mode triggers a 5-10+ minute rebuild that looks like a hang

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. ./b4w.ps1 stop 2. ./b4w.ps1 goto <url> (or any command that auto-starts the server)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: After 'stop', the next command should restart the backend in the documented ~10s-3min window for a source-tree dev setup.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The restarting goto command did not complete within 400s and again within 420s (moved to background twice); the server eventually came UP. AGENTS.md documents first-launch build latency (~1-3 min) but not that every stop/start cycle re-runs a multi-minute bundle build, so the long silence reads as a hang with no progress indication.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The daemon rebuilds/refreshes the backend bundle from source on restart in dev mode; the rebuild duration depends on Maven incremental state and can far exceed the documented first-launch estimate. The CLI prints no progress while the build runs (the spinner/output appears only later).

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/daemon.rs (dev bundle rebuild on restart); b4w.ps1 (startup pipeline)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Print explicit build progress ('Rebuilding backend bundle from source... this can take several minutes') while the daemon rebuilds
- Reuse the last built bundle when source is unchanged (incremental check) so stop/start is fast in the common case
- Update AGENTS.md to state that stop/start cycles re-trigger the build and its real duration

issues.title: Crawl progress output is noisy and uninformative; per-page fetch is slow for small seed sets

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file .test-sessions/seed-urls.txt --depth 0 --sql @.test-sessions/product-query.sql --format table --refresh

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Progress reporting that shows meaningful per-page status and an indication of expected duration.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The same line 'Crawling... 1 pages found so far' repeated ~6 times with no new information, then a single '1/3 seeds done... (86s elapsed)' line; the 3-page crawl took ~96s (~30s/page) — slower than the equivalent swarm (3 jobs finished in ~1.5 min including worker startup) and much slower than AC6's shell loop over the same URLs. For the 'known URLs' case (§4b → crawl --seed-file), a first-time user sees no ETA and no way to tell if the crawl is progressing or stuck.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI's poll loop prints only the cumulative pages-found count on every poll tick regardless of delta, and the backend rate-limits sequential page fetches (intended politeness), which is unbuffered by any UI-level progress estimate.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/http.rs (crawl progress polling output); browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/api/service/CrawlService.kt (per-page pacing)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Only print progress when the count changes, and include per-URL status (fetched/extracted/failed) as each page completes
- Show an elapsed-time and pages/sec figure after the first page completes
- For depth-0 seed crawls, note in the output when parallel swarm would be faster for large seed files

issues.title: swarm --help and main help hide swarm create's flags (display mode, parallelism) behind a second help level

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. ./b4w.ps1 swarm --help 2. ./b4w.ps1 help swarm

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The swarm section should surface --display-mode, --max-browser-contexts, --max-open-tabs (the flags the task's AC4 requires for headless parallelism) so users don't have to open the reference doc.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: swarm --help lists only subcommand names and one-line descriptions; the create flags appear only in ./b4w.ps1 swarm create --help or in swarm.md. A first-time user following SKILL.md §4b ('parallel → swarm') must guess to run 'swarm create --help' to discover the parallelism controls.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The help renderer for subcommand groups shows only subcommand summaries, not each subcommand's options; swarm create's options are documented but not surfaced in group-level help.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (swarm group help rendering)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Include a compact options block for key subcommands (create/query) in swarm --help, at minimum the parallelism and display-mode flags
- Or add a 'Common flags' line to the swarm group header: 'swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS --max-browser-contexts N --max-open-tabs M'
